name: C11-2
question: Should Hong Kong tighten rent control on subdivided units? Take a position and defend it with evidence from the course archive.

turns.text: I don't know anything about this topic yet and have no essay started. Can you give me a shortlist of sources about rent control on subdivided units in Hong Kong?

You've said you're starting from scratch on rent control for subdivided units in Hong Kong. Before any source can help, what should it do for you — back up a specific claim, show a counter-view, define a term, or give a first-hand case — and which claim or question in your essay would it be serving?

It should define what a subdivided unit is and give me some context on the current rent control scheme, so I understand the basics before I take a position. I don't have a specific claim yet — I need background first.

Here are some places to look, in no particular order:
- D9: Legal Opinion: Compensation and Judicial Review Risk (Legal opinion). Legal opinion by counsel assessing judicial review and compensation risk of rent caps, not background on SDU definitions.
- D6: Working Paper: Rent Control and Supply Elasticity in Marginal Housing (Academic working paper). Academic working paper reviewing elasticity literature and modelling scenarios, assumes economics knowledge, not introductory.
- D1: Subdivided Housing in Hong Kong: A Primer (Policy brief). Policy brief primer defining SDUs and outlining the 2021 ordinance, written as neutral background overview.
- D11: NGO Report: Rehousing Pathways First (NGO report). NGO report presenting survey findings and arguing for rehousing over rent caps, an advocacy vantage point.
- D2: SDU Rent and Stock Index, 2019–2025 (excerpt) (Data excerpt). Data excerpt of stock and rent index 2019-2025 with methodology caveats, figures only, no definitions.
Pick one or more (by id) and tell me why.
It is a neutral primer that defines subdivided units and explains the 2021 ordinance, which is exactly the background I need before forming a position.
